sources.quote: On February 19, 2026, you initiated a voluntary recall of the two semaglutide API batches distributed in the United States.
sources.searcher_note: Primary record for the Harbin recall detail only; letter says recall initiated Feb 19, 2026 (lead says 2026-02-13). Nothing on DMF counts.

sources.quote: FDA recommended that Jixianglong recall the batches, leading the company to pull the API from the U.S. market in February.
sources.searcher_note: Trade press on the Harbin warning letter and recall; no mention of drug master file counts or a filing rush.

sources.quote: Specifically, Chinese company Harbin Jixianglong Biotech Co., Ltd (Harbin) was found to have purchased knock-off semaglutide from a non-Green List facility that was not registered with the FDA.
sources.searcher_note: Post-cutoff (Sept 2026) 20-state AG coalition release naming Harbin; nothing on DMF counts.

sources.quote: 8 India-based manufacturers with an active filing of 61 worldwide
sources.searcher_note: Supplier directory counting 61 manufacturers worldwide with an active semaglutide filing; a directory count, not a DMF-by-year rush, different definition.

sources.quote: The FDA either physically inspected or conducted remote regulatory assessments of 48 GLP-1 API sites and found that nearly one-fifth were not compliant under section 501 of the FD&C Act.
sources.searcher_note: Pattern/context: crowd of GLP-1 API sites FDA had to vet for the green list; not a DMF filing count.

notes: No source found reports the core finding: a count of semaglutide drug master files by filing year, 83 since 2023, or a comparison to past waves since 1980 (tirzepatide 40, esomeprazole 36). PharmaCompass DMF listing pages returned 403 and could not be quoted; C&EN 'Looming GLP-1 drug patent expirations draw generics firms' (Dec 2025) returned 406 and could not be checked. The Harbin recall is covered widely, but the FDA letter dates the recall start Feb 19, 2026, not Feb 13 (the enforcement-report date may differ). Washington Examiner piece on Harbin is paywalled and not recorded. Tennessee AG release (2026-09-23) failed to load.
